\chapter{It Depends, and What Would Have Been}
\label{ch:ur-it-depends-and-what-would-have-been}
\hlchaptermodality{275}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say what something depends on (yih mausam par munhasir hai), say what would be or would have been (agar vaqt hotā, to maiṅ ātā), and tell a short story in six written lines.}

Complete UR-R275-depends-and-would: say what something depends on, and what would have been.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منحصر} (munhasir)}{منحصر (munhasir)}]{\ur{منحصر} (munhasir) — dependent}

\label{lesson:UR-C275-munhasir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say \textquotedblleft{}on one condition\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{ek shart par}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}the weather\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{mausam}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منحصر}}
\textbf{\ur{منحصر}} — \emph{munhasir} — \textquotedblleft{}dependent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{موسم} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih mausam par munhasir hai.} — \textquotedblleft{}It depends on the weather.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

What it depends on takes \textbf{\ur{پر}} (\emph{par}), \textquotedblleft{}on\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{ہے}} closes it.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{سب} \ur{کچھ} \ur{آپ} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sab kuchh āp par munhasir hai.} — \textquotedblleft{}Everything depends on you.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{منحصر}} (\emph{munhasir}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{munḥaṣir}, \textquotedblleft{}confined, limited\textquotedblright{}. Urdu uses it with \textbf{\ur{پر}} for \textquotedblleft{}dependent on\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{munhasir}, then \emph{yih mausam par munhasir hai}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}It depends on you\textquotedblright{} — \emph{yih āp par munhasir hai}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \textbf{\ur{منحصر}} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Dependent\textquotedblright{}.) \textquotedblleft{}It depends on the weather\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{موسم} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے} (par munhasir hai)}{پر منحصر ہے (par munhasir hai)}]{\ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے} (par munhasir hai) — it depends}

\label{lesson:UR-C275-par-munhasir-hai}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}it depends on the weather\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{yih mausam par munhasir hai}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}if it rains\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{agar bārish huī}.) A question often gets this answer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: it depends on …}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih munhasir hai.} — \textquotedblleft{}It depends.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{کیا} \ur{آپ} \ur{کل} \ur{آئیں} \ur{گے؟}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kyā āp kal āeṅ ge?} — \textquotedblleft{}Will you come tomorrow?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{کام} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih kām par munhasir hai.} — \textquotedblleft{}It depends on work.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ur{یہ}} (\emph{yih}), \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}, is the plan in question; what decides it takes \textbf{\ur{پر}}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{پیسوں} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih paisoṅ par munhasir hai.} — \textquotedblleft{}It depends on the money.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: it depends on whether …}
When a whole question decides it, \textbf{\ur{اس} \ur{پر}} (\emph{is par}) stands for it, and \textbf{\ur{کہ}} (\emph{ki}) brings the question:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{اس} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے،}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih is par munhasir hai,}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{کہ} \ur{بارش} \ur{ہو} \ur{گی} \ur{یا} \ur{نہیں۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ki bārish ho gī yā nahīṅ.} — \textquotedblleft{}It depends on whether it will rain or not.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{اس} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے،}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih is par munhasir hai,}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{کہ} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{کب} \ur{جائے} \ur{گی۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ki gāṛī kab jāe gī.} — \textquotedblleft{}It depends on when the train leaves.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}It depends on the weather\textquotedblright{} — \emph{yih mausam par munhasir hai}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}It depends on the money\textquotedblright{} — \emph{yih paisoṅ par munhasir hai}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}It depends on Sara\textquotedblright{} — \emph{yih Sārā par munhasir hai}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}It depends on work\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{کام} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے}}.) And before a whole question? (\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{اس} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے} \ur{کہ}} …)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اگر} \ur{وقت} \ur{ہوتا} (agar vaqt hotā)}{اگر وقت ہوتا (agar vaqt hotā)}]{\ur{اگر} \ur{وقت} \ur{ہوتا} (agar vaqt hotā) — what would have been}

\label{lesson:UR-C275-agar-vaqt-hota}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}it depends on the weather\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}it depends on whether it will rain\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{yih mausam par munhasir hai}, \emph{yih is par munhasir hai ki bārish ho gī yā nahīṅ}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}if it rains, we'll stay at home\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{agar bārish huī, to ham ghar par raheṅ ge}.) That may still happen. This lesson is for what did not.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: -\ur{تا} in both halves}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{میں} \ur{آتا۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ātā.} — \textquotedblleft{}I would come.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Alone, with no \textbf{\ur{ہوں}} (\emph{hūṅ}) after it, \textbf{\ur{آتا}} (\emph{ātā}) is not \textquotedblleft{}I come\textquotedblright{}: it is \textquotedblleft{}I would come\textquotedblright{}, or \textquotedblleft{}I would have come\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{اگر} \ur{وقت} \ur{ہوتا،}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar vaqt hotā,}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{آتا۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{to maiṅ ātā.} — \textquotedblleft{}If I had time, I would come.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Both halves take \textbf{-\ur{تا}} with nothing after it, and each follows its own subject: \textbf{\ur{ہوتا}} for \textbf{\ur{وقت}}, \textbf{\ur{آتا}} for me. The story around it says whether this is now or then.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: with \ur{نہ}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{اگر} \ur{بارش} \ur{نہ} \ur{ہوتی،}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bārish na hotī,}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{جاتے۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{to ham jāte.} — \textquotedblleft{}If it hadn't rained, we would have gone.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ur{نہ}} (\emph{na}), not \textbf{\ur{نہیں}}, says \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} here, as in \textbf{\ur{نہ} … \ur{نہ} …} (\emph{na … na …}).

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{اگر} \ur{میں} \ur{جلدی} \ur{اٹھتا،}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar maiṅ jaldī uṭhtā,}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ur{تو} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{نہ} \ur{چھوٹتی۔}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{to gāṛī na chhūṭtī.} — \textquotedblleft{}If I had got up early, I wouldn't have missed the train.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If I had time, I would come\textquotedblright{} — \emph{agar vaqt hotā, to maiṅ ātā}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If I had time, I would go\textquotedblright{} — \emph{agar vaqt hotā, to maiṅ jātā}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If I had time, I would read\textquotedblright{} — \emph{agar vaqt hotā, to maiṅ paṛhtā}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}If I had time\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{اگر} \ur{وقت} \ur{ہوتا}}.) \textquotedblleft{}I would come\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{میں} \ur{آتا}}, or \textbf{\ur{آتی}}.) Which \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} goes with \textbf{\ur{ہوتی}}? (\textbf{\ur{نہ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(six lines)]{Six lines about a trip}

\label{lesson:UR-W275-six-lines}



\begin{quote}
You read Sara's trip to Lahore. Now you write one: a trip of your own, real or invented, for a friend to read.

Say \textbf{\ur{دوران}} (\emph{daurān}) and \textbf{\ur{بعد}} (\emph{bād}) aloud; one of them will go in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
A told story is not a list. It has a \textbf{scene}, with \textbf{\ur{رہا} \ur{تھا}} or \textbf{\ur{جب} … \ur{تو} …}; \textbf{events} in the plain past, kept in order with \textbf{\ur{پہلے}}, \textbf{\ur{پھر}}, \textbf{\ur{اس} \ur{کے} \ur{بعد}}, \textbf{\ur{آخر} \ur{میں}}, and joined with \textbf{\ur{کر}}; a \textbf{reason}, with \textbf{\ur{کیونکہ}}, \textbf{\ur{اس} \ur{لیے}} or \textbf{\ur{کی} \ur{وجہ} \ur{سے}}; and a \textbf{feeling}, with \textbf{\ur{مجھے} … \ur{لگا}} or \textbf{\ur{میں} \ur{خوش} \ur{ہوا}}. It can end on what might have been: \textbf{\ur{اگر} … \ur{ہوتا،} \ur{تو} …}.

\subsection*{Writing — connected composition}
On paper, in Urdu script, write \textbf{six lines}, one for each frame. Each line is one short sentence of your own; the frame gives its job, not its words.

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item where you went, and when: \textbf{\ur{کل} \ur{میں} … \ur{گیا}} (or \textbf{\ur{گئی}}), or \textbf{\ur{پچھلے} \ur{ہفتے}} …;
  \item the scene as you set off: \textbf{… \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا}}, or \textbf{\ur{جب} …\ur{،} \ur{تو} …};
  \item what happened first and next: \textbf{\ur{پہلے}} …\ur{،} \textbf{\ur{پھر}} …\ur{،} or a \textbf{\ur{کر}} form; one thing done with \textbf{\ur{نے}};
  \item one thing that went wrong, why, and whom you told: \textbf{\ur{کھو} \ur{گیا}}, \textbf{\ur{چھوٹ} \ur{گئی}} or \textbf{\ur{حادثہ}}, with \textbf{\ur{کیونکہ}} or \textbf{\ur{کی} \ur{وجہ} \ur{سے}}, and \textbf{… \ur{کو} \ur{بتایا}};
  \item how it ended and how you felt: \textbf{\ur{آخر} \ur{میں}} …\ur{،} \textbf{\ur{مجھے} … \ur{لگا}} or \textbf{\ur{میں} \ur{خوش} \ur{ہوا}}, or what you hope now: \textbf{\ur{مجھے} \ur{امید} \ur{ہے} \ur{کہ}} …;
  \item what might have been: \textbf{\ur{اگر} … \ur{ہوتا،} \ur{تو} …}, with one word that holds a letter you wrote in these chapters: \ur{ع}, \ur{غ}, \ur{ذ}, \ur{ث}, \ur{ڈ}, \ur{ص} or \ur{ؤ}.
\end{enumerate}

There is no model in this lesson. Use only words you already write.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read your six lines aloud. Mark each past verb \textbf{s} for scene and \textbf{e} for event: line two mostly \textbf{s}, lines three and four mostly \textbf{e}.

Then three checks. A plain past with an object has \textbf{\ur{نے}} on its doer and follows the object: \textbf{\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{ٹکٹ} \ur{لیا}}, \textbf{\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{چائے} \ur{پی}}. A \textbf{\ur{رہا} \ur{تھا}} verb takes no \textbf{\ur{نے}}. In line six, do both halves end in \textbf{-\ur{تا}}?
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — it depends, and what would have been}

\label{lesson:UR-R275-depends-and-would}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}if it rains, we'll stay at home\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}or else\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{agar bārish huī, to ham ghar par raheṅ ge}, \emph{varnā}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}since yesterday\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}in my view\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{kal se}, \emph{mere khayāl meṅ}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item Will you come tomorrow? It depends on the weather.
  \item It depends on whether it will rain or not.
  \item If I had time, I would come.
  \item If it hadn't rained, we would have gone.
  \item If I had got up early, I wouldn't have missed the train.
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}It depends on you\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ur{یہ} \ur{آپ} \ur{پر} \ur{منحصر} \ur{ہے}}.) Now the other way round: in \textbf{\ur{اگر} \ur{وقت} \ur{ہوتا،} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{آتا}}, did I come? (No.) Which form do both halves take? (\textbf{-\ur{تا}}, with nothing after it.)
\end{tcolorbox}
